person: Lan Tran is a 41-year-old pharmacy technician who works rotating shifts at a chain pharmacy. Before that she worked at a county hospital pharmacy. She took a 31,400-dollar consolidation loan for her pharmacy technician program and thinks she has been paying toward loan forgiveness for years, but she is not sure how many months count. She has a teenager starting college and her mother lives with her. She reads official English slowly, wants short plain steps, and asks first whether anything costs money. She once paid a helper who did nothing useful, so she will not accept hidden fees.
stated_up_front: Hello. I pay my student loan for many years and I work at hospital before. Can you check how many months count for the forgiveness, and tell me if anything cost money?

facts.truth: One consolidation loan of 31,400 dollars for her pharmacy technician program. She pays about 190 dollars a month on an income-based plan.
Valley County Hospital pharmacy, a government employer. She worked there full time, 36 hours a week, from June 2016 to January 2021, and has a W-2 for each year.
A chain pharmacy, full time since February 2021 on rotating shifts. Her hours were cut to 26 a week in July 2026. It is a for-profit company.
Since 2022 she gets a 150-dollar monthly stipend from the pharmacy workers' union for being a shop representative. She has a stipend letter in her email.
Since 2023 she interprets Vietnamese two evenings a week for Hoa Sen Refugee Center, a nonprofit. She is paid on a 1099 form, not as an employee.
She asked her servicer for two months of forbearance, March and April 2024, when her mother moved in and money was short.
The tracker shows 53 qualifying months. She thinks the hospital job alone should give about 56 before the payment pause months.
She finished her program in June 2015 and the loan went into repayment in December 2015. She made no payments during those six months.
Hospital W-2s and the offer letter are in Gmail. She kept the paper letters about earlier certification in a folder at home and has not scanned them.
She does not want to pay for any buyback or any helper unless Athena tells her the exact amount first and she says yes.

unknowns: Whether the union stipend job counts as a qualifying employer
Whether the 1099 interpreting work counts toward forgiveness
What the forbearance code on her payment history means for the count
The deadline for asking the Department to reconsider a month
Which month her count will reach 120
